origin: 2026-09-02 Codex group-chat session. A user asked whether a viral tweet about the Dutch Box 3 tax on savings was real; the assistant rated its factuality 45/100.

evidence_down.evidence_note: Real. Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS), 'Belastingdruk huishoudens gedaald van 15 naar 12 procent sinds 2011', 2026-09-09, https://www.cbs.nl/nl-nl/nieuws/2026/37/belastingdruk-huishoudens-gedaald-van-15-naar-12-procent-sinds-2011. The tweet says the state takes 'about half before you can save anything'; the fact sheet gives only statutory Box 1 bracket rates (up to 49.50%), which leave the actual average burden open. New register data showing a median burden of 12.3% of gross household income in income tax and national insurance premiums (24.9% for the top income decile, and 32.3% even with social insurance and pension premiums added) directly contradict 'about half'. Direction changed from up to down: no fact published on or after 2026-07-01 was found that supports the tweet; the Belastingplan 2027 package (2026-09-15) leaves Box 3 unchanged apart from indexation and a higher deemed return on other assets, which does not bear on the tweet's overstatements.
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on 9 September 2026 Statistics Netherlands (CBS) published new household income data for 2024 (provisional figures). The median household paid 12.3% of its gross household income in income tax and national insurance premiums (AOW, Anw and Wlz), down from 15.4% in 2011. Among the tenth of households with the highest gross incomes, the median was 24.9%. When premiums for unemployment, sickness and disability insurance and pension premiums are also counted, the median total tax and premium burden was 32.3% of gross household income. The figures do not include indirect taxes such as VAT. Does that change your rating?
Makes sense. What is your final number?
